own_scenes.family: Nueva York: Def Jam, Queens y la edad de oro
own_scenes.desc: Shawn Carter aprendió con Jaz-O y recorrió las giras de Big Daddy Kane; DJ Clark Kent, convencido de que era «el Jesucristo del rap», dejó dos sellos que no quisieron ficharlo, le montó un estudio en casa y le presentó a Damon Dash, que defendía a su Big L. Con Dash y Kareem «Biggs» Burke fundó Roc-A-Fella (1995) para ser independiente. Reasonable Doubt (1996), rap mafioso de un buscavidas que reflexiona sobre esa vida («D’Evils», «Regrets»), con DJ Premier, Clark Kent, Ski Beatz («Dead Presidents», sobre Lonnie Liston Smith y una frase de Nas) y «Brooklyn’s Finest» con Biggie, que no podía creer que Jay no escribiera las rimas: se convirtieron en rivales y amigos. Iba a ser un solo disco; acabó con catorce números 1, Rocawear, la presidencia de Def Jam y el primer billón del hip hop. Roc-A-Fella, con Just Blaze, Kanye West, Beanie Sigel, Cam’ron, Memphis Bleek o Dipset bajo el mismo techo, se vendió a Island Def Jam en 2004.

refs.q: He was supposed to be independent. He was supposed to control his own destiny. He was supposed to become a billionaire.
refs.para: But you know what? It wasn’t supposed to be. Jay wasn’t supposed to sign to those two labels. He was supposed to be independent. He was supposed to control his own destiny. He was supposed to become a billionaire. If he would’ve been at these places, who knows? It might not have happened the same way.

refs.q: I’m gonna have to take it with me and I’m gonna figure it out.
refs.para: And then he saw it happen in front of him and he was like, “I’m gonna have to take it with me and I’m gonna figure it out.” And then I think it was about two months later, he came back and did the verses right before we were mastering. But it was perfect.

refs.q: And, as the old saying goes, steel sharpens steel.
refs.para: Just Blaze (producer): We had our schedules. [Memphis] Bleek was the early bird. He would be in the studio by ten o’clock ’cause he would like to be out in the afternoon and still have the day. Jay would show up around two. You had the Dipset guys showing up around six. State Property guys would kind of filter in between that, and then Beanie Sigel would show up at like four in the morning because he was a late owl. The real reason for that success was that you had all those creative minds under one roof. And, as the old saying goes, steel sharpens steel.
